what_its_for: Tazemetostat is a cancer medicine used to treat two types of cancer: (1) Epithelioid sarcoma, a rare soft tissue cancer, in adults and children 16 years and older when the tumor cannot be removed by surgery. (2) Follicular lymphoma, a type of slow-growing blood cancer, in adults whose cancer has come back or stopped responding to at least 2 prior treatments. It works by blocking a protein called EZH2 that helps cancer cells grow and multiply.
how_to_take: Take tazemetostat by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, break, or chew them. You may take this medicine with or without food. Take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. If you vomit after taking a dose, do NOT take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 800 mg (four 200 mg tablets) taken twice a day, every 12 hours. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different depending on your situation.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 12 hours away. If your next dose is within 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tazemetostat tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Protect it from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take — especially St. John's Wort, antifungals (like fluconazole or ketoconazole), antibiotics (like rifampin), seizure medicines, or HIV medicines, as many drugs can interact with tazemetostat. Women who could become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose. Men with female partners who could become pregnant should use condoms during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: new or unusual lumps or growths anywhere on your body (this medicine may rarely cause new cancers called secondary T-cell lymphomas or myeloid cancers); unusual tiredness or weakness; easy bruising or bleeding; fever, chills, or signs of infection; shortness of breath; rapid or unexplained weight loss; swollen lymph nodes; nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain that is severe or does not go away; or any other new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Tazemetostat starts working right away at a cellular level, but you may not notice changes in your symptoms for several weeks or months. Your doctor will schedule regular check-ups, blood tests, and scans to monitor how well the medicine is working. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use during pregnancy. Use effective birth control as described above. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Children: Tazemetostat is approved for patients 16 years and older for epithelioid sarcoma. It has not been fully studied in younger children. Older adults (65+): May be used but watch closely for side effects. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
